newsitem.title: CHINA: China smelters remain short, no large zinc sales.
newsitem.headline: China smelters remain short, no large zinc sales.

text.p: Chinese smelters continue to hold large net short positions in zinc and have not been selling the metal on a scale that could impact on the London Metal Exchange (LME) contract price, which fell dramatically in early trading on Tuesday, Chinese industry sources said.
China's short position on the LME, said to be up to 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes, has not been closed out and so was not the reason for the falls, trading sources in China, Hong Kong and Singapore said.
"I can't really say what our position is but it is still there," a source at a major Chinese smelter said.
He and other traders said zinc's crash was due to selling by Western banks and trading houses cashing in at levels that reached seven-year highs near $1,700 a tonne on Monday.
LME three months zinc dived $170 in the space of 30 minutes on Tuesday morning, amid fund selling and general liquidation, traders in London said.
Some light speculative Chinese selling accompanied the fall, traders said.
"These falls are good for us because it means the margins (on our short position) will be narrower," said a source at the Zhuzhou smelter in central China.
Zhuzhou is said to have a short position on the LME of around 90,000 tonnes, out of the total Chinese position that Chinese officials have said is about 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes.

The forward contracts were sold earlier this year when the zinc price was around $1,100 a tonne on the advice of Beijing's central metals producing arm China National Nonferrous Metals Corp (CNNC), according to a recent report in an industry magazine, China Metals, published by the official Xinhua

But several South Korean base metal dealers, contacted by Reuters in Seoul, had a contrary view to their regional counterparts and said Chinese zinc smelters seemed to have unwound most of their short positions by Monday, which prompted the funds to liquidate.
"Right after the London market opening today, one trader in London said Chinese smelters had covered most of their open positions by yesterday," said a dealer with a futures brokerage firm in Seoul.
"It was the reason why the cash-to-threes backwardation had widened to $100 a tonne yesterday," he said.
The trader said he expected the zinc backwardation would shrink significantly on the LME on Tuesday.
